title: Grateful Dead Live at Olympia Theater on 1972-05-04

ai_review.summary: Excellent SBD recording captures a high‑energy show highlighted by a smoking Dark Star and superb Good Lovin', with crystal‑clear mix and standout Pigpen moments.
ai_review.review: The performance is a smooth, flowing marathon that starts a bit slow but erupts into a monster second set featuring an unforgettable Dark Star, blazing Good Lovin' and inspired Pigpen organ work. The soundboard source delivers a clean, well‑balanced mix that lets every nuance shine, from Jerry’s rare‑form guitar on Jack Straw to Billy’s stellar drum solo.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of detailed reviews rate the show 5 stars, praising both musical peaks and the pristine soundboard mix; only one moderate rating mentions a slow start, resulting in an overall very high average.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clean, crisp mix with balanced instrument levels; reviewers note “nice mix”, “clean sound off the board” and “SBD quality”. No major drop‑outs or noise reported.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Early set is a bit sluggish, but the band gains momentum and delivers a seamless second set with tight transitions, especially the Dark Star jam and the high‑energy Good Lovin' opener.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for being in rare form; his guitar on Jack Straw is called a favorite ever and he “lifts the band higher” during Dark Star.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ chops are highlighted as a special West‑Coast sound, adding a sweet texture throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Drums: Billy’s drum solo is repeatedly called one of his best—hot from start to finish and a centerpiece of the Dark Star.
